maria_cs: Drafting a lightweight customer-facing runbook for onboarding -> go-live focused on caching/batching/streaming + renewal signals. Sharing for feedback and to align enablement cadence. TL;DR: prefills + warm pools, progressive batching, streaming fallback, renewal-risk checkins.

dan_engineer: love the TL;DR. can you paste the short checklist here? easier to comment inline.

maria_cs: sure — pasted below. please keep replies short, we need a version for CS playbooks and a separate one for Solutions Eng.

---RUNBOOK DRAFT START---
Purpose: reduce first-hour errors, minimize token cost, and surface early renewal risk signals during onboarding.
1) Warmup & Prefill:
  - Prefill requests: send 3 deterministic short prompts per model variant (5–20 tokens) during tenant warmup to populate KV cache.
  - Warm pools: request customer to enable warm pool (if Dedicated) or run 2 warmup passes within first 30 mins (hosted).
  - Telemetry: mark warmup events with tag `onboard:warmup_v1` so CS can query effects.
2) Batching & Concurrency:
  - Start with conservative concurrency (<=2 per instance), then ramp to production concurrency by day 3.
  - Use small micro-batches for interactive flows (batch size 2–4) to keep latency below SLO.
3) Streaming fallback:
  - If 95th p50 latency > 800ms or backend errors spike, flip to streaming-only mode for that route (circuit-breaker flag).
  - Provide client snippet sample:```js
  // client: enable streaming fallback
  fetch('/v1/generate', {headers:{'X-Fallback-Stream':'true'}})
  ```
4) Renewal & Health signals:
  - Capture `prefill_success_rate`, `avg_first_response_ms`, `failed_requests_1h`.
  - If prefill_success_rate < 85% after first 4 warmup attempts, tag account as `onboard:at-risk` and notify CS.
5) Feedback loop & enablement cadence:
  - CS check-in #1 (T+1 day): confirm warmup & client integration, capture samples.
  - CS check-in #2 (T+7 days): confirm batch sizing and latency trends.
  - Ask engineering for a 30-min tuning session if `at-risk`.
---RUNBOOK DRAFT END---

sophia_support: two quick notes: 1) we should add a short template for what to ask customers to reproduce issues (browser, SDK, sample prompt). 2) include how to redact PII in prefill logs.

lee_sre: add a step to auto-roll back to smaller model variant (quantized) after 3 consecutive spool-up failures. otherwise warm pools can eat GPU slots.

ben_ops: for Dedicated customers, call out the billing annotation for warmup traffic so finance doesn't flag it as abuse. small tag: `warmup:unbilled=true` in the telemetry metadata.

anya_pm: this looks good. two product asks: can we make the streaming fallback opt-out for clients that can't handle partial answers? also add a one-sentence explainer for Sales enablement on why prefill reduces tokens.

maria_cs: @sophia_support added a repro template section (one-liners) and a PII redaction note. @lee_sre and @ben_ops added the rollback and billing tags — thanks.

maria_cs: updated runbook snippet for Sales one-liner: "Prefill warms the model and caches common prefixes so downstream requests are faster and cheaper — customers see latency improvements within minutes."

dan_engineer: small nit: the client snippet should show header name we actually accept: X-Redwood-Fallback (not X-Fallback-Stream). also maybe give a curl example for CS to run during calls.

maria_cs: updated header name and added curl example below.

maria_cs: ```bash
# curl quick fallback test during onboarding call
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Fallback: true" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}'
```

oncall-bot: Incident alert suppressed: warmup-run triggered for tenant acme-inc (warmup_events=3) — no errors.

maria_cs: next steps: 1) finalize doc for CS playbook (short checklist + repro template + curl snippet) 2) create Solutions Eng deep-dive with telemetry queries and playbook screenshots 3) schedule 30m sync with SRE and ENG next Wed. who can join?
